---
title: "The Working Draft"
---

::: {.landing}
:::

This book collects two teaching notes that were written separately and belong together. The first, on scientific writing, grew out of workshops I have been running for doctoral students at the Faculty of Medicine of the University of Porto since the early 2010s. The second, on data visualisation, started as a companion piece: the images that sit between the words. Both were published individually on [tiagojacinto.eu](https://tiagojacinto.eu) and used in teaching before any thought was given to combining them.

The case for combining them is straightforward. A figure is part of a paper. A paper is more than its figures. The same person makes both sets of decisions, for the same readers, under the same editorial pressure.

It is written for three overlapping readers: doctoral students in clinical research, doctoral students in health data science, and medical undergraduates taking their first steps into research. Prior statistical exposure helps but is not assumed; terms are defined on first use and collected in the [glossary](chapters/glossary.qmd). Every principle is followed immediately by an example, and the examples run through the same simulated cohorts across the book, so the visual choices, the writing choices, and the analysis can be read against each other.

Part I is the architecture and craft of scientific writing. Part II is the decisions that produce a figure worth looking at. Part III is the analysis beneath the paper: reporting a clinical prediction model to the standard such models are held to, and making code and data reproducible enough that another researcher can rerun them.

**How to read it.** Writing a paper now: read Part I in order. Data but no draft: start with [why writing matters](chapters/01-why-writing.qmd), [clear writing](chapters/03-clear-writing.qmd), and [the writing workflow](chapters/09-workflow.qmd). New to research: those first two, with the [glossary](chapters/glossary.qmd) open. Working in data and code: Part III. Part II reads independently at any stage. The [quick reference](chapters/guide.qmd) and the [checklists](chapters/checklists.qmd) are there for when you need one answer fast, and the [worked example](chapters/worked-example.qmd) assembles the whole book into one short paper.

Tiago Jacinto\
Porto, August 2026
